welcomeOfferTitle.message: 👋 New here? Take the five-minute setup tour

welcomeOfferBody.message: Six short steps: create your vault, back up your sync code, connect your own cloud, bring in your browser's passwords, and meet the two transfer tabs. You can stop and come back any time — the tour remembers where you were.

aw0Body.message: This machine runs UCrypt $1 (build $2…). On your OTHER machine, open UCrypt → Settings → Security → “Owner acceptance & release identity” and check the same version and build. Both machines must run THE EXACT SAME VERSION — that is what makes this test mean anything.

aw0Fix.message: If the versions differ: install the same release on both machines before continuing — every later step depends on it.

aw0Confirm.message: Both machines run the same version

aw1Body.message: Sign in to your Google Cloud console once. Check: the Drive API is enabled, your OAuth client exists, and the publishing status is “In production” (the Testing status expires keys and breaks sync weeks later — publishing to production is the one-time fix).

aw1Fix.message: If the console shows “Testing”: press “Publish app” on the consent screen — no verification review is needed for a personal app only you use.

aw1Confirm.message: The console is checked (or my cloud needs no console)

aw2Title.message: Step 2 — the ladder on this machine

aw2Body.message: Open Cloud Sync and look at your transport: the Sign-In Ladder shows which rung you are on. Fast (one click, where your browser allows) → Guided (your own key, illustrated walkthroughs) → Manual (paste a token). Press “Verify my setup” to see the rung rows.

aw2See.message: What you should see: the transport card names its rung; the Verify rows show one ladder line per transport, and a connected transport never shows a red row for a missing fast rung.

aw2Fix.message: If nothing is connected yet: press Connect on the Cloud Sync tab — one click where your browser allows it, or follow the guided walkthrough (the “Show me how” link) with your own key.

aw2Confirm.message: The rung state is visible and truthful

aw3Title.message: Step 3 — the join (from your other machine)

aw3Body.message: On your OTHER machine, generate the sync code (Cloud Sync → “Create sync code”), then paste it below to check its shape. The check stays in this box — nothing is stored. Then open the Join wizard here and paste it for real: the arrival line names your cloud and the ladder appears.

aw3Placeholder.message: Paste the 24-word code (or the m: pairing line)

aw3InputHelp.message: The check is local-only: it reads the shape (word count / m: prefix) and forgets the words.

aw3See.message: What you should see: the Join wizard's arrival line — “attached to your cloud”, the transport named, the ladder block in view.

aw3Fix.message: If the arrival line never appears: the code may have a typo (a checksum mismatch names it), or the cloud was not pushed yet — run “Sync now” on the other machine first.

aw3Skip.message: Skip this step (finish the join later — recorded honestly)

aw4Body.message: On your OTHER machine, create a new entry (any site, any username). Watch THIS machine: within a moment (a save, a pull, or the 15-minute cycle) the same entry appears in the vault list here.

aw4See.message: What you should see: the new entry appears here without you touching anything — that is the crossing you are confirming.

aw4Fix.message: If it never appears: press “Sync now” here once. If it still never appears, the cloud leg is the suspect — run “Test connection” on both machines and note which side errs.

aw4Confirm.message: The entry crossed and appeared here

aw5Body.message: On your OTHER machine, change one setting that syncs (for example the auto-lock time or a clipboard preference). Watch this machine apply the same change on its next pull.

aw5See.message: What you should see: the setting matches on both machines after a pull — no manual copying.

aw5Fix.message: If the change never travels: some settings are device-local on purpose (the transport choice itself, for one). Try a different setting and note which one refused — that is a finding worth reporting.

aw6Body.message: Direct Share sends a file to any UCrypt user with NO chain, NO cloud, NO account: you mint an invitation, they accept it, one hop, done. If they are offline when the invitation is about to expire, the card offers to hold the file for pickup on YOUR cloud — one click, and they pick it up later with a code. Mint one from the Direct Share tab and receive it on the other machine (or with a friend).

aw6See.message: What you should see: the share code travels through any messenger; the receiver accepts and the file arrives digest-verified. The share can never join your chain — that separation is structural.

aw6Fix.message: If the handshake stalls: both sides must keep the window open until the transfer completes; the invitation expires after 10 minutes by design — mint a fresh one.

aw7Title.message: Step 7 — rename both ways + a tab transfer

aw7Body.message: Rename one entry here and see the rename arrive on the other machine; rename there and see it arrive here. Then send a small file from the Device Transfer tab (files move between YOUR synced devices, end-to-end encrypted, no cloud copy).

aw7See.message: What you should see: renames travel both directions; the transfer lands with a digest check.

aw7Fix.message: If a rename collides with an edit on the other side, UCrypt keeps BOTH (tombstones, never deletes) — the resolution line names it. A stalled transfer: both windows open, then retry.

aw7Confirm.message: Renames crossed; the tab transfer landed

aw8Body.message: Bring your browser's own passwords in: Export / Import → “Take your stuff with you” walks the CSV drop with a preview and ONE confirm. The CSV lands nowhere but the vault — delete it from your Downloads after the import (the wizard reminds you).

aw8See.message: What you should see: the preview names the count; one confirm saves them; the entries sit in the vault and sync from now on.

aw8Fix.message: If your browser refuses to export a CSV: every browser hides it behind its own settings search (“passwords”) — the wizard links each browser's exact page.

aw8Confirm.message: An import landed in the vault

aw9Title.message: Step 9 — the self-check and the summary

aw9Body.message: Capture the self-check one last time, then copy the summary: it lists every step as ok / skipped, any findings in the step · expected · observed shape, and the exact build both machines ran. It carries NO secrets — paste it as your re-test report.

aw9See.message: What you should see: the summary text below — structured, honest about skipped steps, and scan-clean.

aw9Fix.message: If Copy is blocked by the browser, select the summary text and copy it manually — the panel never hides it.

wl0Body.message: UCrypt keeps your passwords and 2FA tokens in an encrypted vault that lives in THIS browser and syncs to YOUR own cloud — nobody's server in the middle. Set a master passphrase and you are in.

wl0See.message: What you should see: the Vault tab with your (for now empty) list, ready for its first entry.

wl0Fix.message: If you are locked out: the master passphrase has no recovery — that is the point. Use Emergency wipe and start fresh; your data was only what you had already.

wl1Title.message: Your sync code — back it up

wl1Body.message: The 24-word sync code is the ONE key to your cloud copy: lose the browser and the code restores everything. Write it on paper and keep it safe — a password manager that syncs should never gatekeep its own backup.

wl1See.message: What you should see: Cloud Sync → “Create sync code” shows 24 words and a copy button.

wl1Fix.message: If you already have a code (restoring a device): press “I already have one” instead — the words pull your vault down from your cloud.

wl1Confirm.message: My code is written down somewhere safe

wl2Body.message: UCrypt seals your vault and stores it in YOUR Google Drive, Dropbox, GitHub Gist or any WebDAV server. The Sign-In Ladder gives you the fastest sign-in your browser allows, illustrated guided steps for your own key, and a manual paste — your cloud, your rules.

wl2Fix.message: If the fast one-click is not offered: that is the honest graceful absence — your browser or account setup does not allow it yet. The guided rung always works.

wl2Confirm.message: My cloud is connected (or I know where the door is)

wl3Body.message: Passwords from any browser (the CSV walk), bookmarks, history — the migration wizard previews everything and saves with ONE confirm.

wl3Fix.message: If your browser hides its CSV export: the wizard links every browser's exact settings page.

wl3Confirm.message: My stuff is in (or I will do it later)

wl4Body.message: Device Transfer sends files between YOUR synced devices — no cloud copy. Direct Share sends a file to any UCrypt user through a one-hop encrypted handshake — no chain, no account. Both live in their own tabs, one click away.

wl4See.message: What you should see: the two tabs in the top menu, each with its own audience line.

wl4Fix.message: A transfer that stalls: both sides keep their window open; Direct Share invitations expire after 10 minutes by design — mint a fresh one.

wl4Confirm.message: I know where both tabs are

wl5Body.message: That is the whole tour: vault → code → cloud → import → the two tabs. Copy the summary if you want a record of your setup tour, or just close and start using UCrypt.

wl5Fix.message: If anything feels off: the door is always the same — Cloud Sync for the code and the cloud, Export / Import for bringing things in. Nothing in this tour was required to start using UCrypt.
